strong_findings.difference: As for Gasperini-Veneziano 2003: conformal frames of one spacetime, not position/momentum descriptions; primordial inflation inside collapsing regions, not the present acceleration; no conjugate universe and no Λ.

strong_findings.citation: D. Mukherjee, H. K. Jassal, K. Lochan, "Bouncing and collapsing universes dual to late-time cosmological models", Eur. Phys. J. C 84 (2024) 318, arXiv:2207.02835 (2022)
strong_findings.summary: Uses the Einstein-frame/Jordan-frame (conformal) correspondence of scalar-tensor gravity to give the dark-energy-driven late universe a dual description: a ΛCDM Einstein frame always maps to a bouncing Brans-Dicke Jordan frame, and quintessence plus matter to a Jordan-frame turnaround, a bounce or a collapse. The abstract concludes that the effect of dark energy can equivalently be seen as collapse of space in a conformally connected universe. Two passages beyond the abstract bear on C5's route. Sec. 6 runs the map the other way: a de Sitter Jordan frame (Brans-Dicke parameter -4/3), which mimics the dark-energy-dominated era, has as its Einstein-frame dual a stiff fluid (w = 1, zero potential, a purely kinetic scalar) that contracts toward a crunch. That is the pairing of #11 §10's 'dual stiff ↦ Λ' with the stiff side contracting, realized in another duality. Sec. 5.2's thawing example uses the hilltop potential Λ⁴(1 + cos(φ/f)), the functional form of #11's τ potential V₀[1 + cos(τ/f)], and arranges the Jordan-frame collapse at the current era, which bears on the open question of how the route relates to τ's potential.
strong_findings.difference: The dual description is a conformal (Weyl) rescaling of the same spacetime in a scalar-tensor theory, fixed by the Brans-Dicke field, not the momentum-space description of Born reciprocity, and no relation like a·ã = 1 holds (in sec. 6 the Einstein-frame scale factor goes as (1 - const·t̃)^(1/3) while the Jordan one grows exponentially, eq. 47). Dark energy (Λ, quintessence or the Brans-Dicke field) is put in by hand in one frame; the collapse in the other is a re-description ('equivalently', 'alternatively'), not its source, so C5's 'drives' is absent, though #11 App. A item 8 reads its own duality as synchronized, not causal. The turnaround point is tunable through the Brans-Dicke parameter, and for ΛCDM the dual is a bounce, not a collapse. The stiff/de Sitter pairing of sec. 6 is one exact solution (ω_BD = -4/3, U = 0), not a dictionary w_eff = -w̃. Not anticipation: the conjecture's partner is the momentum-space (conjugate) description, and here it is a conformal frame. The g4 verifier reported this paper (g4-collapse-acceleration/verify.json, new_findings; it read the abstract and secs. 3 and 8); it is not in round3/known.json. Sec. 6 and the sec. 5.2 hilltop example are not in that entry.

When our scale factor is the smaller one (a << 1) our universe follows a ~ 1/t² in the background time, which 'translates into a t² evolution in standard comoving coordinates', an acceleration without dark energy, while the conjugate scale factor 1/a shrinks. strong_findings.summary: Dark Gravity treats the metric g and its 'inverse' g̃ = η g⁻¹ η as two faces of one field (a 'Janus field'), each with its own matter. In the cosmological sector the two scale factors are inverses, ã(t) = 1/a(t), and the paper states that our side's expansion means the dark side is contracting. After a postulated discontinuous permutation of the two scale factors at the transition redshift, the dark side's source term dominates and drives our evolution, giving a constantly accelerated expansion a(t′) ~ t′² with no cosmological constant (the paper's single parameter replacing Λ is the transition redshift, predicted 0.78 against a measured 0.67 ± 0.1). The conjugate world is the inverse metric of a flat-background theory, related to ours by a global time-reversal/permutation symmetry, not the momentum-space (Born-reciprocal) description of our universe. The acceleration comes from the anti-gravitating action of the dark side's cold matter once a discontinuous scale-factor permutation has made its source term dominant, not from gravitational collapse of the conjugate universe and not from dual kinetic energy carried across as Λ by w_eff = −w̃; the dark side contracts throughout, including our decelerating era. The result is power-law acceleration a ~ t′², not a cosmological constant.

strong_findings.citation: H. Wu, H. Yang, "Double Field Theory Inspired Cosmology", JCAP 07 (2014) 024, arXiv:1307.0159
strong_findings.summary: Cosmological solutions of double field theory, which doubles space into ordinary coordinates x and dual (T-dual) coordinates x̃. In the solution with an O(D,D)-invariant dilaton potential the dual scale factor is the inverse of the ordinary one, a₂ = a⁻¹, so the dual space contracts while ordinary space expands. The authors state that the contraction of the dual space causes the ordinary space first to inflate (accelerate) and later to expand at a decelerating rate. A later DFT paper (Y. Liu, Gen. Rel. Grav. 54 (2022) 18, arXiv:2112.15082) summarizes the result as 'the contraction of the conjugated space leads to both an inflation phase and a decelerated expansion of the ordinary space'.
strong_findings.difference: Same causal wording as C5 (contraction of the dual space, with the inverse scale factor, accelerates our space), but for primordial inflation, not the present acceleration. The dual space is the winding (T-dual) coordinate space of double field theory, not the momentum-space polarization of a Born-reciprocal theory. The driver is dilaton dynamics with an exponential potential; no matter content, no collapse of a conjugate sector, no dictionary entry such as dual stiff → Λ. The same contraction also produces the later decelerated expansion, so in this paper contraction alone does not fix the sign of the acceleration; with a₂ = a⁻¹ the 'causes' is a kinematic identity of one solution.

strong_findings.citation: M. Gasperini, G. Veneziano, "Inflation, deflation, and frame independence in string cosmology", Mod. Phys. Lett. A 8 (1993) 3701, arXiv:hep-th/9309023
strong_findings.summary: The origin of the pre-big-bang identification that the searcher found in Gasperini-Veneziano 2003 and Buonanno-Damour-Veneziano 1999. String-frame inflationary solutions suggested by scale-factor duality are accelerated contraction ('deflation') in the Einstein frame, and the virtues of inflation have 'physically equivalent counterparts in the deflationary (Einstein-frame) picture'. One process, two descriptions: accelerated contraction in one is accelerated expansion in the other.
strong_findings.difference: Conformal (Weyl) frames related by the dilaton, not position and momentum with a·ã = 1; primordial inflation, not the present acceleration; the contraction is our own universe's Einstein-frame metric, with no conjugate matter and no dictionary; superinflation, not Λ.

strong_findings.citation: M. Gasperini, G. Veneziano, "The pre-big bang scenario in string cosmology", Phys. Rept. 373 (2003) 1, arXiv:hep-th/0207130
strong_findings.summary: In pre-big-bang cosmology one evolution is described in two conformal frames. A superinflationary (accelerating) expansion in the string frame is an accelerated contraction in the Einstein frame, where the dilaton is a massless scalar minimally coupled to gravity (kinetic-dominated, a stiff fluid) that cannot inflate but 'can easily lead to gravitational collapse'; section 3.3 is titled 'Pre-big bang inflation as gravitational collapse'. Section 2.2 also gives the scale-factor duality with sources, attributed to Veneziano 1991: a_i → a_i⁻¹ with the shifted density ρ̄ = ρ √−g preserved and the shifted pressure reversed, which 'reflects' the barotropic equation of state γ → −γ. This is the same map as the program's corrected dictionary w_eff = −w̃ (#11 section 10), which carries the energy per comoving volume across unchanged; under it a stiff fluid (γ = 1) goes to γ = −1.
strong_findings.difference: The two descriptions are the string and Einstein conformal frames, related by the dilaton, not position and momentum related by Born reciprocity; the collapse is of our own universe as seen in the other frame, not of a conjugate one; the acceleration is primordial superinflation (growing H), not the present epoch and not a cosmological constant. The duality with sources is an exact symmetry of string-frame dilaton gravity, whereas the program derives w_eff = −w̃ in Einstein gravity from a·ã = 1 with one shared lapse; the paper never applies γ → −γ to dark energy. Read with C5's route, it states the same structure: a contracting, kinetic-dominated universe in one description is an accelerating universe in the other.

not_found_statements.statement: C5 in its own terms: the momentum-space (Born-reciprocal, conjugate-polarization) description of our universe, whose scale factor is the inverse of ours (a·ã = 1), contracts as ours expands, and its gravitational collapse is what drives our present accelerated expansion. No paper found states this. The configuration (inverse scale factor, contracting partner, partner drives present acceleration) appears only in Dark Gravity, with a different partner and mechanism; the causal phrase 'contraction of the dual space ... inflation' appears only for primordial inflation (Wu-Yang 2014); dark energy sourced on the momentum or dual side appears without any contraction (Bolognesi 2012/2015; Berglund-Hübsch-Minić 2019; Hur et al. 2025; Ran 2026).

The route the record keeps: a stiff (kinetic-dominated) fluid in a dual, conjugate or contracting sector acting on our expansion as a cosmological constant (dual stiff → Λ) as an explanation of present dark energy. The map itself exists in the literature as scale-factor duality with sources (γ → −γ, Veneziano 1991 via Gasperini-Veneziano 2003 eq. 2.32), and pre-big-bang cosmology identifies a collapsing stiff Einstein-frame universe with string-frame inflation, but no paper found applies the stiff → Λ entry to late-time dark energy.

C5 in its own terms, in venues outside INSPIRE and arXiv as well as inside them: no work found states that the momentum-space (Born-reciprocal, conjugate-polarization) description of our universe, with a·ã = 1, contracts as ours expands and that its gravitational collapse drives our present accelerated expansion. Searched here: 25 OpenAlex searches over titles, abstracts and full texts (dual, mirror, twin, conjugate, anti-, parallel/shadow/partner universe; momentum-space universe; Born reciprocity; scale-factor duality; stiff/kinetic-dominated + Λ + duality; inverse scale factor; expansion-collapse duality; full-text phrases such as 'collapse of the dual universe', 'momentum space contracts', 'conjugate universe'), 8 Crossref searches (6 thematic, 2 lookups), 3 Zenodo searches (one further call rejected for page size) and 2 HAL searches, 10 WebSearch queries (8 extended), with the INSPIRE citation graph around the closest find. The closest statement anywhere is Mukherjee-Jassal-Lochan (EPJC 2024): dark energy is 'equivalently' the collapse of a conformally connected (Jordan-frame) universe, a different duality with dark energy assumed. Outside the journals, the configuration 'a contracting partner universe tied to our dark energy' appears only in non-reviewed Zenodo deposits (Stolt 2025; Alshareif 2026), without a mechanism and, in Alshareif, with the opposite causal arrow.

The route the record keeps, dual stiff ↦ Λ applied to late-time dark energy in a Born-reciprocal or momentum-space setting: not found. The pairing itself (a contracting, purely kinetic stiff-fluid description dual to a de Sitter, dark-energy-like description) appears as one exact solution in Mukherjee-Jassal-Lochan 2024 sec. 6, in Einstein/Jordan conformal frames of Brans-Dicke gravity (ω_BD = -4/3), not as a dictionary entry and not as the source of acceleration. No non-arXiv source was found that applies stiff ↦ Λ to dark energy (OpenAlex stiff/kination + Λ + dual/duality: 4 irrelevant hits; full text stiff + scale-factor duality + Λ/dark energy: 9 hits, whose abstracts do not apply it (string and teleparallel cosmology, bounces, theses on pre-big-bang and T-duality; full texts not read); Crossref and WebSearch extended: none).

The wording 'their collapse is our acceleration' (or 'conjugate gravitational collapse drives positional expansion acceleration'): no occurrence found (WebSearch exact phrase: essays on accelerationism only; OpenAlex full-text phrase search drops the stopwords and cannot test it).

No lineage paper states that the gravitational collapse or contraction of a momentum-space (conjugate) description of our universe drives our accelerating expansion, or that stiff (kinetic-dominated) content of such a description acts on ours as a cosmological constant. Nearest analogs: a second matter population's clustering or repulsion (Manfredi, Rouet, Miller 2026; Petit and d'Agostini 2014), collapse of our own structures (Räsänen 2006, outside the assigned lineages), and dark-energy terms from momentum- or velocity-space geometry (Hazboun-Wheeler, Moffat, pseudo-complex GR, Ibadov-Murodov, kinetic-gas Finsler gravity, tangent-bundle cosmology, Carmeli).

Holds in C5's own terms: the verifier's 20 searches found no paper in which the momentum-space (Born-reciprocal) description of our universe, with a·ã = 1, contracts and its collapse drives our present acceleration. Two corrections to the statement's supporting sentence. (a) The link between collapse in a dual description and accelerated expansion is not confined to primordial inflation: Mukherjee, Jassal and Lochan (JCAP 2021; EPJC 2024) state, for the present epoch, that the dark-energy-driven expansion is equivalently a collapse of a conformally connected (Jordan-frame) universe, though as a re-description of assumed dark energy, not as its source. (b) Read kinematically, Dark Gravity's accelerated regime is the inverse of a collapsing dust conjugate universe (radiation-like in the hot case), so it holds the founding image in a different framework. Bolognesi 2012/2015, Berglund-Hübsch-Minić 2019, Hur et al. 2025 and Ran 2026, with Castro 2012/2020 and Triantafyllopoulos-Stavrinos 2018, place dark energy on the dual or momentum side without any contraction; they are related, not partial.

Holds for the entry itself: no paper found applies 'dual stiff -> Λ' to late-time dark energy. The entry is scale-factor duality with sources (Veneziano 1991; Gasperini-Veneziano 2003 eq. 2.32), now checked algebraically to equal the program's corrected dictionary for d = 3 (verifier's script, step 7). Qualification: the route's structure (a contracting conjugate universe of suitable contents acts on ours as a cosmological constant) appears in Dark Gravity under its conformal-time dictionary (w + w̃ = -2/3), where the suitable content is radiation, not stiff matter: a radiation-like contracting conjugate side gives our de Sitter expansion. The review ties that phase to an inflation-like epoch, and the 2018 proceedings mention 'another scenario leading to an exponential acceleration' without detail.
